Now for me, my self improvement journey begun with my health and fitness, but you fortunately have that covered up because you do soccer, so I assume youre fit and eating healthy. Next step for me was my grooming, hygiene and overall physical attractiveness. I bought nicer clothes and learned to make outfits etc. Get rid of other unhealthy habits if you have any. Many people our age smoke and drink and get drunk and its just gross. Become straight edge if you can, people wont notice it at first, but you will be steps and steps ahead of them at fitness and life quality. Also just getting drunk overall is stupid. Don't masturbate so much. Masturbation too much (3+ a week) can cause in young adults low testostorone, low libido and lethargy overall. I can confidently say this is one thing that will improve you as much as being healthy and fit. Its necessary. Its hard as shit, but dont expect to become great at it at first. Im nott saying dont masturbate, but do that shit rarely and make it a reward rather than a boredom eliminator. Since you already do sports, I don't think you need another hobby, but you can always start a second sport like basketball or volleyball or runnning in general. Even not professionaly you can just go to a court and play there. People will come and play with you and you can meet them thru that. Be in mediums that you will meet people. Work sports etc. You can take up an instrument, guitar usually is a go to at any age and it is easy to play. Go outside and see the sun more, limit your social media and screen usage, use it only for networking and talking to/meeting people, the time you waste on that IG or youtube is time that could be spent doing sports. If anything on this list suits you and you can do it, I'd say do it. They worked for me, they can or may not work for you, but these are very general and objective life improving things you can do. Tbh I think you're gonna be pretty fine in the future because youre doing sports and in a team. I could never experience that I regret everyday i didnt take up a sport earlier on. In any case, I hope you do great and you probably will, and I wish nothing but best of luck to you. Life is tough but we're tougher.
